newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Zastava to outline transformation - institute.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Zastava to outline transformation - institute.

text.p: The Belgrade-based Economics institute said on Monday it would outline a privatisation programme for Serbia's car maker Zastava by the end of the month.

"The institute is preparing a model for the ownership transformation and restructuring of personnel in the Zastava car factory," said Vlada Poznanic, leader of the institute's team commissioned to prepare the programme.
"We expect the programme to be finalised and accepted by the end of January," he told Reuters.

Zastava's 1996 production of about 10,000 vehicles was well below original plans of 27,000 vehicles, but was 1,500 vehicles up against the production in 1995 when sanctions against Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, were still in force.
"Our plan for 1997 is very optimistic," Zastava spokesman Zvonko Osrecki said. "We estimate our production to reach 30,000 vehicles out of which half is to be exported."
Despite the lifting of sanctions and a government financial injection, the factory has failed to revive production due to lack of capital and financial problems faced by its domestic suppliers.
"Lack of finances in Zastava and its sub-contractors was the main reason for such a shortfall in production," Osrecki said.

Hurt by the break-up of former Yugoslavia and almost four years of crippling U.N. sanctions, Zastava's production fell to a mere 20,000 vehicles over the 1991-1995 period from its annual capacity of about 200,000 in pre-war years.
